title: William Hoy and Hoy’s Station
summary: William Hoy established Hoy’s Station in Madison County in 1781, about six miles northwest of present-day Richmond, with help from George Boone.
bodyMarkdown:
William Hoy established Hoy's Station in [Madison County](https://grokipedia.com/page/Madison_County,_Kentucky) in 1781, with help from George Boone, according to a Boone-family genealogy. A Filson Historical Society study of pioneer forts and stations places it about six miles northwest of present-day Richmond. It was one of a ring of small stations that grew up near Boonesborough in the years of the Revolution.

A station in those years was a cluster of cabins joined by a stockade, built so a few families could farm by day and shelter together at night. Settlers cleared fields, raised corn, and kept watch. Raiding parties from the north crossed the Ohio often, and anyone working outside the walls could be taken or killed.

In 1782 that danger fell on two boys. Wyandot warriors captured Jones Hoy and Jack Calloway near Boonesborough. Capt. John Holder gathered 17 militiamen and went after them. On August 12, 1782, Holder's party overtook the band on Great Salt Creek, as the Licking River was then called. In the skirmish Holder lost four men and, outnumbered, withdrew without the boys.

Jones Hoy was held captive for seven years before he came home. Jack Calloway was held for a shorter time. The fight at the Upper Blue Licks was soon overshadowed: only days later, on August 19, a larger Kentucky force was beaten at the [Battle of Blue Licks](/stories/battle-of-blue-licks/) farther down the same river.

Little else about the station's later years is recorded. Like many early stations, it likely faded as the frontier quieted and families moved out onto their own farms.

## Kentucky today

The Kentucky Historical Society's Upper Blue Licks marker in Nicholas County records Holder's skirmish but does not mention the station or say how the boys were tied to it. The map pin uses the USGS historic-locale point for William Hoy's Station, an approximate site. Holder's own story is told in [John Holder at Lower Howard's Creek](/stories/col-john-holder-at-lower-howards-creek/).
Source: [Upper Blue Licks marker (Kentucky Historical Society)](https://history.ky.gov/markers/upper-blue-licks)
Source: [Kentucky Pioneer Forts and Stations (Filson Historical Society)](https://filsonhistorical.org/wp-content/uploads/publicationpdfs/76-4-6_Kentucky-Pioneer-Forts-and-Stations_Hammon-Neal-O..pdf)
